definition: Chinchilla is a family of large language models (LLMs) developed by the research team at Google DeepMind, presented in March 2022.
details: Chinchilla is a family of large language models (LLMs) developed by the research team at Google DeepMind, presented in March 2022.

explainer.lead: Chinchilla is a family of large language models from Google DeepMind's research team, presented in March 2022. Its name identifies a particular line of language-model research rather than a general modeling technique.

tiers.eli5: Chinchilla is a family of computer models made to work with language. Think of it like a surname shared by several related models rather than the name of one single machine. It was presented by researchers at Google DeepMind in March 2022.
tiers.practitioner: Treat Chinchilla as a model-family name, not as a complete specification of a deployable system. Work that depends on a particular checkpoint, interface, or configuration needs more detail than the family name and presentation date provide.
tiers.paperLevel: Chinchilla denotes a family of large language models developed by the research team at Google DeepMind and presented in March 2022. The term therefore refers to a set of related models rather than an architecture, algorithm, or benchmark.

explainer.example: When cataloguing Google DeepMind's language models by presentation date, Chinchilla would be listed as a model family presented in March 2022.
explainer.origin: Chinchilla was developed by the research team at Google DeepMind and presented in March 2022.
explainer.whyItMatters: Chinchilla provides a specific name for a family of large language models in Google DeepMind's research history, helping distinguish it from other models and modeling ideas.
